name: Pi3
plain: π3 (Pi3, yyfz): cameras, depth and 3D points from many unposed images in one pass, with no reference view. Non-commercial weights.
summary: π³, permutation-equivariant visual geometry learning (Wang et al. 2025): cameras, depth and point maps of every view from unposed images in one forward pass, with no reference view. A DINOv2 ViT-L/14 encoder feeds 36 alternating frame / global attention blocks (q/k norm, 2-D RoPE); three small transformer decoders give local point maps, confidences and camera poses.
licence_notes: The Pi3 code is BSD-3-Clause, but the README licenses the Pi3 weights CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial); the Hugging Face card's bsd-2-clause tag is overridden by that statement.
limitations: With CUDA float16, stream=True keeps the 36 frame and global attention blocks in pinned host RAM. The image encoder, prediction heads and activations stay on the GPU. Export requires stream=False.
An experimental replacement for the camera rotation SVD exported at two 224 x 336 views. TensorRT 11.4 failed to finish building within 220–228 seconds with both default and level-0 optimization.

The standalone FP16 TensorRT encoder for eight 512 x 640 views took 735 ms end to end with eager decoding. On five DTU scans, relative L2 change was at most 0.49% for world points and 0.038% for the camera matrices.
task_io: Input: several images of one scene (posed and calibrated for multi-view stereo, unposed otherwise). Output: depth maps and, where the model predicts them, cameras and 3-D points.

quality.title: DTU scans 1, 9, 24, 33, 75, view 24 + 7 sources, AbsRel / delta1 %
quality.protocol: 640x512 crops, the 7 most co-visible views as sources. Ground truth is depth rendered from the structured-light points. AbsRel / delta1 over GT pixels, after per-image median scaling unless the model takes the cameras (calibrated MVS: cameras, error in mm; PatchMatchNet also the depth range 425-935 mm, MVSAnywhere its own range from the camera baselines).

tensorrt.note: The fixed eight-view FP16 DINOv2 encoder runs with TensorRT. Decoding, camera estimation and point reconstruction run in PyTorch.

quality.title: DTU (five scans), view 24 + 7 sources at 336 x 518, AbsRel
quality.protocol: Resize the eight DTU images to 336 x 518 and the reference depth with nearest-neighbor sampling. Align the predicted depth by median scale on valid reference pixels before averaging AbsRel over the five scans.

tensorrt.note: TensorRT runs 34 scene-decoder blocks in one fixed FP16 plan. The image encoder, final two decoder blocks, depth and camera heads run in PyTorch. Five DTU scenes, 336 x 518. Relative depth uses median alignment on valid reference pixels.

portable.note: Portable FP16 reference run paired with the standalone TensorRT decoder across the same five DTU scenes.
